trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the affordable ADO bus from the airport to the Hotel Zone (around $5 USD) to reach Cancun Beach Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to the nearest public beach access point to get your first feel of the Caribbean Sea. Relax on the sand, take a dip, and unwind after your flight. Explore the immediate area around the hotel on foot to locate nearby convenience stores and budget eateries.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hotel Zone boulevard at sunset to soak in the atmosphere. Head to a local mercado or budget taqueria near the hotel for a relaxed first dinner in Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — look for OXXO convenience store options.
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable tacos or tortas from a street food stand near the hotel zone for around $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or a local taqueria near the hotel zone — budget around $8–12 USD for tacos, rice, and a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 11:00 AM, don't plan any major activities in the morning. Focus on settling in. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (Telcel or AT&T Mexico) for affordable data. Keep airport transfer costs low by using ADO bus instead of taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for the Playa Delfines Sunrise Beach Walk. Head to one of Cancun's most iconic and completely free public beaches at sunrise (around 6:30–7:00 AM). Enjoy the uncrowded shoreline, stunning turquoise water views, and the famous Cancun sign for photos. This is one of the best free experiences in Cancun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a late breakfast, then head to Playa Tortugas for the Parasailing & Water Sports experience. Try parasailing (approx. $45–60 USD) or opt for more budget-friendly options like renting a kayak or snorkel gear. The beach is lively and fun with plenty of free activities like swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Playa Tortugas or a nearby beach bar. Walk along the Hotel Zone and browse the shops before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab fruit, yogurt, or pan dulce from a local OXXO or Super Chedraui supermarket — budget $3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a casual beachside palapa restaurant near Playa Tortugas — look for a lunch special (comida corrida) for $6–10 USD.
meals.dinner: La Parrilla on Yaxchilan Avenue in Downtown Cancun — authentic Mexican food with great value, budget $10–15 USD including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is accessible via the R-1 or R-2 public bus along Kukulcan Boulevard for just $0.80 USD — one of the best budget transport options in Cancun. Bring sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and cash for street vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the public bus to Downtown Cancun (El Centro) and explore the Mercado 28, a colorful local market where you can browse handcrafted souvenirs, textiles, and authentic Mexican goods at bargain prices. Practice your haggling skills for the best deals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Playa Caracol or Playa Langosta, two free public beaches in the Hotel Zone that are less crowded on weekdays. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the calm Caribbean waters. Bring a book or snorkel gear rented cheaply nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head back downtown to Parque Las Palapas, a lively local square where families gather, street performers entertain, and affordable food stalls serve authentic Yucatecan dishes. A great way to experience local Cancun culture.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a downtown loncheria (small local diner) near Mercado 28 — try huevos rancheros or chilaquiles for $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Grab fresh ceviche or a fish taco plate from a market stall inside Mercado 28 for $5–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food at Parque Las Palapas — try marquesitas (crispy crepes with cheese and fillings), elotes, and tacos for $4–7 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: The public bus (R-1) runs the entire length of Kukulcan Boulevard and into downtown for under $1 USD each way — use it daily to save significantly on transport. Mercado 28 opens around 9:00 AM. Bring small bills for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Isla Mujeres via ferry from Puerto Juarez (ferry costs approx. $8–10 USD each way — much cheaper than Hotel Zone ferries). Arrive early to beat the crowds and rent a golf cart ($40–50 USD for the day, split among travel companions) or explore by foot and local moto-taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Playa Norte on Isla Mujeres, consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean. The water is shallow, calm, and crystal clear — perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Explore the colorful streets and art of the island village.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the last ferry back to Cancun (ferries run until around 8:30–9:00 PM). Relax at the hotel or grab a light dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bakery for $3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant on Isla Mujeres away from the tourist strip — try fresh grilled fish or shrimp tacos for $8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Keep it simple with street tacos or OXXO snacks near the hotel after returning — budget $4–6 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Take the public bus to Puerto Juarez ferry terminal (much cheaper than Hotel Zone ferries to Isla Mujeres). Bring cash, sunscreen, a towel, and snorkel gear if you have it. The island is very walkable if you skip the golf cart rental to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at Playa Delfines again or explore a new stretch of beach along the Hotel Zone. Collect shells, take photos, and enjoy the peaceful morning atmosphere before the beach fills up. Consider a free yoga session on the beach if available through your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Cancun Scenic Overlook at Playa Delfines for panoramic views of the Hotel Zone and lagoon. Then head to a cenote day trip — take a budget combo tour to Cenote Azul or Cenote Cristalino near Playa del Carmen (shared tours from $25–35 USD including transport), or visit the more accessible Cenote Chikin Ha.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun for a festive Friday night. Head to Coco Bongo area or the Forum by the Sea to enjoy the free outdoor atmosphere and street performers. Window shop and enjoy the buzzing Hotel Zone nightlife without spending on cover charges.

meals.breakfast: Make your own breakfast with groceries from Chedraui supermarket — fruit, bread, and juice for $4–6 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the supermarket to enjoy at the cenote — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks for $5 USD.
meals.dinner: Try Tacos y Mariscos El Paisano or a similar local seafood taqueria in the Hotel Zone for $10–14 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in the Hotel Zone are lively and fun to explore for free. If doing a cenote trip, book a shared shuttle tour the night before for the best rates. Bring a waterproof bag and underwater camera or phone case for the cenote.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final sunrise or early morning swim at the beach near your hotel. Pack your bags and do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 23 in downtown Cancun (smaller and more local than Mercado 28, with very affordable prices on crafts and snacks).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, spend your last afternoon relaxing at a free public beach or taking a final stroll along the Hotel Zone. Return to the hotel to collect luggage and check out. Take the ADO bus back to the airport ($5 USD) for a budget-friendly departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Cancun International Airport. If your flight is late evening, grab a final meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before heading through security.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a sit-down breakfast at a local café near the hotel — try molletes or enfrijoladas for $5–8 USD as a farewell Mexican meal.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable lunch at Mercado 23 — fresh juice, tacos, and fruit for $5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final taco from a street stand near the airport — budget $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 PM — ask the hotel to store your luggage if your flight is later in the day. Keep $50–100 USD cash on hand for the last day's expenses. Confirm your departure terminal and allow extra time for airport security on busy Saturday departures.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort in the Hotel Zone. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort amenities and nearby surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll along the Hotel Zone beachfront directly in front of the resort. Dip your toes in the turquoise Caribbean water, relax on the beach, and decompress from travel. Explore the immediate area and pick up any essentials at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant close to the hotel. Try La Fisheria or a similar local seafood spot in the Hotel Zone for fresh ceviche, fish tacos, and Caribbean-style dishes to kick off the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — airport café or terminal food court.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort restaurant or a casual beachside café upon arrival — try a fresh fruit plate, guacamole, and chips.
meals.dinner: La Fisheria or similar Hotel Zone seafood restaurant — budget approx. $20–$35 USD per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight arrives at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 relaxed. Check-in is typically at 3:00 PM — ask the resort to store luggage if the room isn't ready. Arrange any activity bookings for the coming days at the concierge desk this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Sunrise Beach Walk — wake up early and head to one of Cancun's most beautiful and uncrowded public beaches at sunrise. Playa Delfines is about a 10-minute taxi ride south along the Hotel Zone. Enjoy the peaceful morning light, walk the shoreline, and take in the iconic Cancun sign for photos before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a late breakfast, then spend the afternoon at Playa Tortugas for Parasailing & Water Sports. Head to lively Playa Tortugas in the Hotel Zone for an exciting afternoon — try parasailing for panoramic views of the Caribbean coast, or choose from jet skiing, banana boat rides, or paddleboarding. The beach has plenty of vendors and a fun, energetic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at a rooftop or open-air restaurant in the Hotel Zone. Puerto Madero or Labná are excellent mid-range options offering Mexican cuisine with a lively ambiance. Afterward, take a relaxed evening walk along the Hotel Zone's main boulevard, Kukulcan.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack before the sunrise walk (granola bar, fruit from a resort shop), then a proper breakfast at the resort buffet or a café upon return — approx. $10–$15 USD.
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at Playa Tortugas — fresh tacos, grilled corn, or a seafood platter from one of the beach restaurants — approx. $12–$18 USD.
meals.dinner: Labná or Puerto Madero — traditional Mexican or Argentine-style grill — approx. $25–$40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and cash for water sports vendors at Playa Tortugas (many prefer cash). Parasailing typically costs $50–$70 USD per person. Book in advance or on-site. Taxi from hotel to Playa Delfines is roughly $5–$8 USD each way.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Catamaran Day Trip — depart early from Puerto Juárez or Playa Tortugas ferry dock for a full-day catamaran excursion to the stunning Isla Mujeres. Sail the turquoise Caribbean waters, snorkel in coral-rich reefs teeming with tropical fish, and enjoy an open bar and snacks on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the charming, colorful island on foot or by golf cart (rentals available for ~$40 USD/hour). Visit the soft white sands of Playa Norte, browse artisan shops along the main pedestrian street, and soak up the laid-back island vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Return by catamaran or ferry to Cancun in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant. Tonight is a good night to rest early after a full day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — buffet or continental — approx. $12–$18 USD or included with stay.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included on the catamaran excursion (buffet-style on the boat or at a beach club on Isla Mujeres). Confirm with tour operator.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby spot like Surfin' Burrito or Harry's — approx. $18–$30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Catamaran day trips typically cost $60–$90 USD per person and include snorkel gear, open bar, and lunch. Book through the resort concierge or a reputable operator like Asterix or Captain Hook. Bring biodegradable sunscreen to protect the reef, a light cover-up, and sea sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling Day Trip — depart by rental car or shared shuttle (~1.5 hours south on Highway 307) to Akumal Bay, famous for its resident green sea turtle population. Snorkel in the calm, shallow bay alongside wild sea turtles and colorful reef fish. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat crowds and get the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, enjoy the beautiful Akumal beach and have lunch at one of the local restaurants. On the drive back north, consider a brief stop at the town of Playa del Carmen for a stroll along 5th Avenue (Quinta Avenida) — a vibrant pedestrian street lined with boutiques, cafés, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon. Freshen up at the resort, then enjoy a nice sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the Hotel Zone. Try Elefanta or a similar spot for a mix of international and Mexican flavors.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the resort before the early departure — continental or buffet style.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Akumal — La Buena Vida beach bar or Turtle Bay Café & Bakery offer fresh seafood, sandwiches, and smoothies — approx. $15–$22 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Hotel Zone restaurant such as Elefanta or Kiosco — approx. $22–$35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Entry to Akumal Bay snorkeling area is free but guided snorkel tours from the beach cost $15–$25 USD and are recommended. Life jackets and snorkel gear rental available on-site. Car rental for the day costs approx. $35–$55 USD or book a shared day-trip shuttle (~$30–$50 USD round trip per person) through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Ha Eco Water Park & Beach — take an early morning shuttle south (~1.5 hours) to Xel-Ha, a stunning all-inclusive natural aquatic park built around a coastal lagoon. Snorkel through the lagoon's interconnected waterways, spot tropical fish and rays, float down the lazy river, and explore the lush jungle surroundings. The all-inclusive entry covers food, drinks, snorkel gear, life jackets, and activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Xel-Ha's many offerings — try the cliff jumping platform, bike the jungle trail, visit the beach area on the Caribbean coast, or simply relax in a hammock over the crystal-clear water. The park is best enjoyed at a slow, exploratory pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun in the late afternoon, tired and sun-kissed. Enjoy a final fun evening with dinner at a lively spot — try Señor Frog's or Coco Bongo area for a festive atmosphere, or keep it chill with a beachside dinner under the stars at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure, or eat upon arrival at Xel-Ha (breakfast included in all-inclusive entry if arriving early).
meals.lunch: Fully included in the Xel-Ha all-inclusive entry — multiple restaurant stations throughout the park serving Mexican cuisine, grilled fish, salads, and more.
meals.dinner: Festive dinner at Señor Frog's Hotel Zone location or a beachside restaurant at the resort — approx. $20–$35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xel-Ha all-inclusive entry costs approx. $80–$110 USD per adult (book online in advance for discounts). Wear water shoes if possible. Bring biodegradable sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are prohibited inside the park. Lockers are available for rent. Transportation can be booked as a combo package with the park entry.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — wake up for one last peaceful walk along the hotel's beach at sunrise. Swim in the warm Caribbean, collect a few shells, and take in the stunning turquoise waters one last time. Return to the resort for a leisurely checkout breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend the last few hours doing light souvenir shopping at La Isla Shopping Mall or Mercado 28 (local market) for authentic Mexican crafts, vanilla, hot sauces, and gifts. Mercado 28 offers better prices and a more authentic local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Cancun International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible week of beaches, snorkeling, and Caribbean adventures!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full buffet or a sit-down meal — approx. $15–$20 USD or included with stay.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the shopping area — a local taqueria or casual café at La Isla Shopping Mall — approx. $10–$15 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the Hotel Zone before heading to the airport — keep it light and simple.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort (typically 12:00 PM). Ask about late checkout if your flight is in the evening — some resorts offer this for a fee or as a courtesy. Keep one set of swimwear accessible for the morning beach walk. Exchange any remaining pesos back to your home currency at the airport or a local exchange booth before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium suite. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon unwinding at the resort's private beach and infinity pool. Explore the resort amenities, arrange a beachside cabana, and enjoy the turquoise Caribbean waters at your own pace. Optional: book a 60-minute couples or solo massage at the resort spa to recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar. Enjoy the golden hour views over the Caribbean. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant to ease into the trip without venturing far.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport lounge before boarding
meals.lunch: La Fisheria or the resort's beachside grill upon arrival — fresh ceviche, grilled fish tacos, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Tempo by Martín Berasategui at Hotel Paradisus Cancun — Michelin-starred Basque-inspired tasting menu with Caribbean ingredients; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with a luxury SUV transfer through the resort. Request early check-in if available. Avoid heavy scheduling on Day 1 to recover from travel fatigue. Confirm spa and dining reservations for the week upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Sunrise Beach Walk — Rise early and head to one of Cancun's most stunning and uncrowded public beaches for a serene sunrise experience. Arrive by 6:30 AM to catch the golden light over the Caribbean. Walk the shoreline, take in panoramic views of the Hotel Zone lagoon, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the crowds arrive. Private guide optional for photography and local insight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a late breakfast, then head to Playa Tortugas for an exhilarating afternoon of water sports. Try parasailing for breathtaking aerial views of the Hotel Zone coastline, followed by jet skiing or banana boat rides. The lively beach atmosphere adds energy after the calm morning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to shower and change. Head out for a premium dinner in the Hotel Zone, followed by optional nightlife exploration at Cancun's upscale venues.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast buffet or à la carte — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Playa Tortugas — fresh seafood platters, grilled lobster tacos, and ice-cold micheladas at a premium beach club
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — world-class cuts, fresh oysters, and an impressive wine cellar with stunning lagoon views

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen for all beach and water activities. Bring cash or card for Playa Tortugas water sports vendors. Book parasailing in advance during peak March season. Playa Delfines is free and public — arrive very early for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Catamaran Day Trip — Depart from Puerto Juárez or the Hotel Zone marina by 9:00 AM aboard a premium catamaran. Sail across the turquoise waters to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Snorkel in crystal-clear Caribbean waters teeming with tropical fish and vibrant coral reefs. Enjoy an open bar and snorkeling equipment included in the premium package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the colorful, golf-cart-friendly island. Visit Punta Sur (the southernmost point of Mexico) for dramatic cliff views, stroll the pastel-painted streets of the village, and browse artisan shops. Relax on Playa Norte, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches, with calm, shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Return catamaran to Cancun by 5:30–6:00 PM. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed evening with a premium dinner featuring fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Onboard catamaran buffet lunch included in the premium package — fresh tropical fruits, sandwiches, and open bar; or dine at Lola Valentina on Isla Mujeres for fresh fish and lobster
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Sunset — iconic Cancun institution famous for Mayan-inspired cuisine, coconut shrimp, and the legendary 'Cocobichuela' dessert in a lush garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the premium catamaran package in advance — look for small-group or private charter options for a more exclusive experience. Bring waterproof camera or GoPro for snorkeling. Isla Mujeres golf cart rentals are available for ~$40–60 USD for a few hours. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — mandatory in Mexican marine parks.

day_by_day.morning: Akumal Bay Sea Turtle Snorkeling Day Trip — Depart early by private luxury van (~1.5 hours south to the Riviera Maya). Arrive at Akumal Bay, world-famous for its resident population of green sea turtles. Snorkel alongside these magnificent gentle giants in their natural habitat. A certified guide will lead a small-group or private tour for the best and most ethical wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, enjoy the stunning Half Moon Bay adjacent to Akumal for relaxed swimming and beach time. Stop at Laguna Yal-Ku, a hidden natural lagoon nearby, for additional snorkeling with colorful fish in brackish water. Explore the charming Akumal village before heading back toward Cancun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed resort evening — sunset swim, spa treatment, or simply lounge on the private beach. Opt for a low-key premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — avocado toast, tropical smoothie bowls, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: La Buena Vida at Akumal — beloved beachfront restaurant with hammock seating over the water, fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and margaritas
meals.dinner: Puerto Madero Cancun — Argentine-inspired steakhouse and seafood on the lagoon, known for premium cuts, fresh catch, and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified, eco-responsible snorkeling guide at Akumal to protect the sea turtles and comply with local regulations. Avoid touching or chasing turtles. Private van transfer recommended for comfort and flexibility. Bring biodegradable sunscreen only. This is a full-day excursion — comfortable water shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Xel-Ha Eco Water Park & Beach — Depart by private transfer (~1 hour south). Spend the full day at Xel-Ha, a breathtaking natural aquatic park built around a coastal lagoon and pristine beach. Snorkel through the lagoon's natural inlet where fresh and saltwater meet, encountering hundreds of tropical fish species. The all-inclusive premium package covers food, drinks, snorkeling gear, life vests, towels, and activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Xel-Ha's offerings — cliff jumping platforms, river tubing, hammocks over the water, and the stunning beach area. Enjoy the lush jungle surroundings and cenote features within the park. Take advantage of the premium lounge areas and open bar for a leisurely tropical afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by 5:30–6:00 PM. Tonight, celebrate the penultimate night with a special premium dining experience and optional nightlife at Cancun's upscale venues.

meals.lunch: All-inclusive gourmet buffet and à la carte dining within Xel-Ha — fresh grilled fish, local specialties, tropical drinks, and fresh fruit stations
meals.dinner: Porfirio's Cancun — legendary Mexican fine dining institution with sophisticated interpretations of traditional cuisine, tableside guacamole, premium tequila selection, and vibrant atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Xel-Ha tickets in advance online for the best pricing — the all-inclusive package is highly recommended. Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory inside the park. Bring a waterproof bag for valuables. Water shoes are useful for the rocky lagoon entry points. Lockers are available on-site. This is a full-day experience — arrive at opening for maximum time.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, luxurious breakfast at the resort. Take one last swim in the Caribbean, lounge on the private beach, or indulge in a farewell spa treatment. Pack and prepare for checkout. Optional: revisit Playa Delfines for a quiet, reflective final beach walk and to collect any last photographs of the stunning coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final lunch at a premium Hotel Zone restaurant. Complete any last-minute souvenir shopping at La Isla Shopping Mall or Kukulcán Plaza in the Hotel Zone. Private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cancun. Enjoy the Cancun airport lounges (American Airlines Admirals Club or Plaza Premium Lounge) for a comfortable pre-flight experience with cocktails and light bites.

meals.breakfast: Grand resort farewell breakfast — full spread with made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Lorenzillo's Cancun — iconic waterfront restaurant on the lagoon, famous for live lobster tanks, premium seafood, and stunning views; a perfect final Cancun meal
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or light bites pre-flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort (standard is 12:00 PM — request late checkout if needed, typically available for premium guests). Arrange private airport transfer the night before. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Cancun airport security and immigration. Keep one carry-on outfit accessible if checking bags. Tip resort staff generously before departure.

query: Cancun beach resort, $3000 couple, 6 days, March 2027, from Dallas
